variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: RabbitMQ is a message broker that accepts messages from publishers, routes them through exchanges, stores routed copies in queues, and delivers those copies to consumers. It lets one service hand work to another without both services being available at the same moment.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Publisher
pairs.detail: The publishing application chooses an exchange, routing key, message body, headers, and durability options.
pairs.explanation: The publishing application chooses an exchange, routing key, message body, headers, and durability options. It owns the event contract and publish error handling.

pairs.label: Exchange
pairs.detail: An exchange does not hold a backlog.
pairs.explanation: An exchange does not hold a backlog. It applies its type-specific routing rule and sends a copy to every matching queue.

pairs.label: Binding
pairs.detail: A binding connects an exchange to a queue.
pairs.explanation: A binding connects an exchange to a queue. Its key or arguments express which publishes that queue wants to receive.

pairs.label: Queue
pairs.detail: A queue stores ready messages, tracks unacknowledged deliveries, and dispatches work to its consumers according to broker policy.
pairs.explanation: A queue stores ready messages, tracks unacknowledged deliveries, and dispatches work to its consumers according to broker policy.

pairs.label: Consumer
pairs.detail: A consumer validates the message, applies one business operation, and acknowledges only when the selected completion contract is satisfied.
pairs.explanation: A consumer validates the message, applies one business operation, and acknowledges only when the selected completion contract is satisfied.

pairs.label: Virtual host
pairs.detail: A virtual host contains exchanges, queues, bindings, policies, and permissions.
pairs.explanation: A virtual host contains exchanges, queues, bindings, policies, and permissions. Use it as a deliberate tenancy and operational boundary, not as a naming prefix.

variants.hint:
Publisher: The publishing application chooses an exchange, routing key, message body, headers, and durability options.

Exchange: An exchange does not hold a backlog.

Binding: A binding connects an exchange to a queue.

Queue: A queue stores ready messages, tracks unacknowledged deliveries, and dispatches work to its consumers according to broker policy.

Consumer: A consumer validates the message, applies one business operation, and acknowledges only when the selected completion contract is satisfied.

Virtual host: A virtual host contains exchanges, queues, bindings, policies, and permissions.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

pairs.label: Direct
pairs.detail: A binding key must equal the publish routing key.
pairs.explanation: A binding key must equal the publish routing key. Use it when the event has one stable category such as payment.failed.us.

pairs.label: Topic
pairs.explanation: Bindings match dot-separated words. * matches exactly one word and # matches zero or more. Use stable semantic words, not database table names.

pairs.label: Fanout
pairs.detail: Every bound queue receives a copy and the routing key is ignored.
pairs.explanation: Every bound queue receives a copy and the routing key is ignored. Use it when all current subscribers intentionally receive every publish.

pairs.label: Headers
pairs.detail: Bindings inspect headers instead of the routing key.
pairs.explanation: Bindings inspect headers instead of the routing key. It can express compound conditions, but topic keys are usually easier to discover and operate.

pairs.label: Receive and validate
pairs.detail: Parse the envelope, require a stable message ID and schema version, and reject permanently invalid data without entering an infinite requeue loop.
pairs.explanation: Parse the envelope, require a stable message ID and schema version, and reject permanently invalid data without entering an infinite requeue loop.

pairs.label: Commit one effect
pairs.detail: Apply the domain mutation and record the message ID in the same transactional boundary when duplicate effects would be harmful.
pairs.explanation: Apply the domain mutation and record the message ID in the same transactional boundary when duplicate effects would be harmful.

pairs.label: Acknowledge success
pairs.detail: Send the acknowledgment only after the completion rule is true.
pairs.explanation: Send the acknowledgment only after the completion rule is true. A channel failure before this point makes redelivery possible.

pairs.label: Bound recovery
pairs.detail: Retry transient failures with delay and limits.
pairs.explanation: Retry transient failures with delay and limits. Dead-letter permanently invalid or exhausted messages with their diagnostic context.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: RabbitMQ is a message broker that accepts messages from publishers, routes them through exchanges, stores routed copies in queues, and delivers those copies to consumers. It lets one service hand work to another without both services being available at the same moment.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Work queue
pairs.detail: Several equivalent consumers share one queue.
pairs.explanation: Several equivalent consumers share one queue. Each queue copy is delivered to one consumer at a time, subject to acknowledgment and redelivery.

pairs.label: Subscriber queue
pairs.detail: Each subscriber owns a separate queue bound to the exchange.
pairs.explanation: Each subscriber owns a separate queue bound to the exchange. A slow analytics consumer does not hold notification messages in the same backlog.

pairs.label: Dead-letter queue
pairs.detail: Rejected, expired, or overflowed messages enter a separate queue for diagnosis.
pairs.explanation: Rejected, expired, or overflowed messages enter a separate queue for diagnosis. It needs an owner, retention limit, alert, and controlled replay path.
